title: What is NELFUND?
content: NELFUND (Nigerian Education Loan Fund) provides student financing for eligible tertiary students, covering institutional charges and/or a monthly upkeep allowance. It is a loan, not a scholarship.

title: Is NELFUND a scholarship or a loan?
content: NELFUND is a loan with real repayment obligations. It is not a scholarship or free government money.

title: How do I apply for NELFUND?
content: Applications are done online through the official NELFUND portal at https://portal.nelf.gov.ng/. You will need your NIN, JAMB number, admission details, matriculation number, and BVN. Follow the portal instructions and the how-to-apply guide on this site.

title: Which link do I use to login or start an application?
content: Use the official NELFUND application portal: https://portal.nelf.gov.ng/. That is the same official destination for logging into an existing account and for starting or continuing an application. Do not use third-party sites that ask for payment or OTP. The public information site is https://nelf.gov.ng/.

title: Who is eligible to apply for NELFUND?
content: According to the official NELFUND FAQ, students who have secured admission into public Nigerian universities, polytechnics, colleges of education, or vocational schools can apply, with proof of admission including name, date of birth, admission details, JAMB number, matriculation number, and BVN. New and existing students in those institutions can apply. Direct Entry students need a JAMB number. Confirm current rules on nelf.gov.ng because phase and institutional coverage can evolve.

title: What can disqualify someone from getting the loan?
content: According to the official NELFUND FAQ, an application may be denied if the applicant: (1) has defaulted on a previous loan from any licensed financial institution; (2) was found guilty of submitting fake or fraudulent documents and dismissed for exam malpractice by a school authority; or (3) was convicted of fraud, forgery, drug offences, cultism, felony, or any offence involving dishonesty. Data mismatches, incomplete institutional records, or failed verification can also block progress even when formal disqualification grounds do not apply. Always confirm current rules on the official website.

title: How much is the upkeep allowance?
content: The currently confirmed upkeep amount is ₦20,000 per month. Treat other figures you see online as unverified until confirmed by an official NELFUND source.

title: Will NELFUND pay my school fees?
content: For approved institutional charges, NELFUND pays the institution directly (not into your personal account). Upkeep, when approved, is paid to your bank account.

title: Do I have to pay NELFUND back?
content: Yes. NELFUND is a loan. Current terms indicate repayment begins two years after NYSC completion for students who participate in NYSC. Confirm your personal terms through official channels.

title: My school is not showing on the portal
content: This usually means the portal could not match your institution record. Check that you selected the correct institution name, that your details match official records, and that your school has submitted student data to NELFUND. See the troubleshooting section for practical steps.

title: My application is pending. What does that mean?
content: Pending usually means your application is still going through verification stages (identity, JAMB, institutional, bank). Check the portal status regularly. Do not repeatedly resubmit. See troubleshooting for escalation guidance.

title: Why was my application rejected?
content: Common causes include mismatched personal details (NIN/JAMB/name), incomplete institutional records, or eligibility issues. The portal should indicate a reason. This guide cannot invent your specific rejection reason. Check the portal and official channels, then use the troubleshooting section for corrective steps.

title: I already paid my school fees. What happens?
content: General NELFUND rules and institution-specific refund procedures can differ. This guide does not have a confirmed official rule covering every institution. Check your institution's student portal or NELFUND liaison office for how credits or refunds are handled.

institution_tips.tip: At OOU, check the student portal and the office handling NELFUND coordination for any notice about fees already paid.

title: Do I need a guarantor?
content: Confirm current guarantor requirements on the official NELFUND portal. Do not pay anyone claiming to provide a guarantor.

title: No school information found
content: This usually means a mismatch between your personal/academic details and the institution's submitted record. Double-check NIN, JAMB, matric number, and name spelling. Contact your institution's NELFUND liaison if the problem persists.

title: Has my school uploaded my record to NELFUND?
content: You cannot see a private NELFUND admin upload log as a student. Practical signs that your record may not yet be matched include: school not appearing, missing information / student records messages, or failed institutional verification. Institutions submit student records on their own schedule. Ask your institution's ICT, Registry, or NELFUND coordination office whether your session cohort has been uploaded, and confirm your details match their records exactly.

institution_tips.tip: At OOU, check the student portal and the office responsible for NELFUND coordination.

title: Can I apply for both school fees and upkeep?
content: Where the portal allows it, you can select institutional charges and/or upkeep. Each component you receive becomes part of the loan you must repay.
